exclusions.reason: The analytic first-harmonic cosine coefficient is zero. Rumoca and OMC both leave integration residue, and Rumoca's residual is closer to zero; OMC's near-zero reference spread makes normalized pointwise comparison non-identifying.

The MSL model is explicitly chaotic and runs for 50000 seconds. Exponential trajectory separation makes one solver's pointwise trajectory non-identifying; this model requires invariant or statistical comparison.

Only switch1.LossPower is non-high (67/68 channels and all initial conditions are high). The ideal switch defines LossPower=v*i and produces the same 2.3247705375e8 W opening spike in both traces, but the independently located sine zero crossing is recorded at t=0.416666833851481 by Rumoca and t=0.416666666694237 by OMC. Pointwise interpolation converts that sub-microsecond coordinate difference on a discontinuous algebraic spike into a severe integral error even though its value and the state trajectories agree, so OMC pointwise comparison is non-identifying for this event-local observable.

At the 0.1 s input step, OMC records the pre-event PIA resistor loss powers at t=0.1 and the post-event values at t=0.1000000001100004, while Rumoca records the post-event values at t=0.1. The post-event peak agrees to floating-point precision and 281/283 channels are strict-high; the two minor channels are aliases of this event-side output convention, so raw pointwise interpolation is non-identifying.

This autonomous relaxation oscillator deliberately wraps the op-amp saturation branch in noEvent, so the MLS does not require event localization at its discontinuous right-hand side. Both traces start from the same state and preserve the analytic 30 V amplitude, but solver-dependent crossing phase accumulates over ten periods (Rumoca's default half-period is about 0.0472 s and OMC's about 0.0495 s); tightening Rumoca converges toward 0.05 s, while OMC at 1e-8 and 1e-10 fails at the hidden discontinuity instead of providing a converged reference. Same-time pointwise comparison is therefore non-identifying; this model requires limit-cycle amplitude/period and phase-aligned waveform obligations.

Only switch1.LossPower is non-high (57/58 channels and all initial conditions are high). The ideal switch defines LossPower=v*i and both traces produce the same approximately 2.466374e8 W opening spike, but Rumoca records the scheduled opening at the exact t=0.5 coordinate while OMC records it at t=0.500000000200003. Pointwise interpolation turns this 2.0e-10 s event-coordinate convention into a deviation on the discontinuous algebraic spike although the state trajectories agree, so OMC pointwise comparison is non-identifying for this event-local observable.

At the 0.1 s current-command step, OMC records the pre-event PID error at t=0.1 and the post-event value at t=0.1000000001100014, while Rumoca records the post-event value at t=0.1. The seven minor channels are PID error aliases of this event-side phase shift; all 200 other channels are strict-high and the post-event response agrees, so raw pointwise interpolation at the discontinuity is non-identifying.

Only four aliases of the two IdealDcDc power-balance residuals are non-high; 586/590 channels and every initial condition are high. These near-zero residuals drive integral controllers with Ti=1e-6 and are dominated by integration error: tightening OMC from 1e-6 to 1e-8 reduces their ranges from 8.18e-3/6.84e-3 W to 7.16e-4/1.92e-4 W, while tightened Rumoca gives comparable 7.83e-4/2.62e-4 W ranges. The default-tolerance OMC residual is not converged enough to identify pointwise parity, while the physical trajectory agrees.

Default OMC reference accuracy is insufficient for this model's near-zero summed currents and pre-closing leakage voltages. With lossless trace decoding, the unchanged Rumoca trace has 690 high, 18 near, and two deviating channels against OMC at the model's 1e-6 tolerance. The same xtask-generated OMC executable at 1e-10 and 1e-12 agrees with that unchanged Rumoca trace on all 710 shared channels; the two refined OMC traces agree on all 735 shared channels. Default OMC's summed star current reaches 9.24e-6 A while Rumoca remains near 1e-13 A, consistent with the SpacePhasor zero-sequence equations. This is a pointwise-reference limitation, not strict-high or certification credit. Source equations, immutable executable/input hashes, and convergence comparisons are recorded in docs/dev-guide/src/tooling/multibody-coverage.md at evidence commit 3d76411c; official tolerances and reference traces are unchanged.

The default OMC reference does not resolve the four zero-sequence voltage observables: SMPM_Braking has 584 high and four deviating channels, with all 588 initial values high. The source and generated OMC equations give vzero=mean(vAC)+3*Rg*i0-mean(rs.v), Rg=1e6; current error is amplified by approximately 3e6 into voltage error. Both original traces satisfy this identity within 7e-8 V. Running the same OMC executable at 1e-9 and 1e-10 reduces the unchanged Rumoca comparison to four near channels, but those two OMC traces themselves have five deviating channels; the 1e-12 diagnostic times out after chattering. There is no converged reference or strict-high claim. An independent analytic stiff RL reproduction at unchanged 1e-6 tolerances has maximum voltage errors of 0.5054 V in OMC and 1.1509 V in Rumoca despite small current errors. This is a conditioned-observable reference limitation; bounding amplified output error remains an explicit numerical accuracy obligation, not certification credit. Source equations, failed diagnostics, and the analytic regression are recorded in docs/dev-guide/src/tooling/multibody-coverage.md at evidence commit 0de3f29c. Official reference traces and tolerances are unchanged.

Only aliases of the period-integrated RootMeanSquare/Mean aggregate differ. At the annotation tolerance of 1e-6, OMC's endpoint RMS is 109.999434852 V; rerunning the same generated OMC model at 1e-10 moves it to 110.000018546 V, a 5.84e-4 V shift that accounts for Rumoca's 5.74e-4 V difference. The physical waveform and state channels agree, so the default-tolerance OMC trace is not converged enough to identify pointwise aggregate parity.

The differing channels are period Mean/RMS aggregates at integration-residue scale within the model's 1e-6 experiment tolerance; waveform channels agree and Rumoca's mean is closer to the analytic 3*sqrt(6)/pi*Vrms value.

The 17 differing channels are all aliases of one degenerate node: the supply star point (sineVoltage.plug_n joined through MultiStarResistance, R=1e6, to ground), which carries zero net current in exact arithmetic so its exact voltage is 0 V; OMC's reference spread is below 1e-9 V. Rumoca's within-tolerance algebraic-loop residual current of order 1e-10 A is amplified by the 1e6 ohm grounding resistance into a broadband 1e-4 V signal that saturates the metric against the 1e-6 normalization floor. All 374 other channels are strict-high (currentSensor.i and voltagesensor.v agree within 1.4e-3 on 13.5 A and 269 V scales) and the rectifier conduction sequence is identical with every switching edge matching within 6e-7 s, so the near-zero reference makes pointwise comparison non-identifying for this node.

The differing meanVoltage.y channel is the event-latched output of Blocks.Math.Mean. Tiny PWM event-time shifts make raw pointwise comparison of the held aggregate non-identifying; the switching waveform and physical states agree, and both solvers converge to the same 19.999995992 V endpoint within 2.7e-10 V.

The default OMC trajectory is not converged under integration refinement: at t=1 s, revolute1.phi is 72.3016881 rad at 1e-6, 48.8580302 at 1e-9, and 48.1459607 at 1e-12. At 1e-12, changing only its fixed initial angle by 1e-8 rad changes the endpoint by 7.1132384 rad. Rumoca and OMC agree on all 5020 state derivatives evaluated at 502 identical OMC points (maximum abs(error)/max(1,abs(reference)) is 1.45e-11), separating equation evaluation from trajectory sensitivity. One default-tolerance OMC trajectory cannot identify pointwise refinement for this sensitive drive train; invariant and sensitivity analysis remain outstanding, and this exclusion is not strict-high certification. Reproduction, source/trace digests, and limitations are recorded in the MultiBody coverage ledger.

Nonsmooth contact-event force and acceleration channels exhibit tiny event-time phase shifts while smooth state and position behavior agree; raw pointwise algebraic acceleration at contact is non-identifying.

The DoubleRamp pump drop-out holds V_flow at exactly zero during t in [0.4, 0.6] s. At exactly zero flow the semiLinear outflow enthalpy observables (pipe T_b, dT, and flowPort h aliases; 9 deviation plus 6 minor of 121 channels, zero severe) are underdetermined by MLS 3.7.4.5 at the model's three-way FlowPort junction, so OMC holds the previous value while rumoca reports a different admissible value. 100.0 percent of every deviating channel's integral error mass lies inside that zero-flow window and the maximum deviation outside it is 2.3e-3 K, while every state (pipe and heat capacitor temperatures) agrees within 1.5e-3 K over the whole 2 s horizon; pointwise comparison of the zero-flow observable is non-identifying.

DoubleRamp starts with exactly zero flow on [0, 0.2] s. The three-way FlowPort junctions leave connector h unconstrained there: TwoPort uses semiLinear(m_flow, connector.h, medium.cp*T), with no fixed connector h initialization. OMC chooses 288.15 and rumoca chooses 0; T_a/T_b=h/cp and dT/dTCoolant aliases account for all 17 deviation channels of 117. This is a non-identifying initial algebraic gauge, not a physical temperature initialization error: all five states initialize identically, and tapT=1 makes T_q=T independently of those aliases. At commit 456f1619, the unchanged xtask comparator on the retained suffix [0.201,1] s, including flow reversal, gives all 117 channels bounded L1 below 0.001115 (high threshold 0.05). Full-horizon state and heat-flow differences are at most 0.001727 K and 0.003453 W. The finite near-zero reversal is not an additional exclusion. Source and suffix provenance are recorded in infra/verification/fluid-review.md. This model remains excluded and non-strict-high; the suffix diagnostic does not certify the full trace.

The only non-high channel is the ideal-diode Boolean diode.off (41 of 42 channels high, including diode.v at bounded-L1 0.0054). For about a third of the run the diode sits at its complementarity knee (diode.v near 1.3e-18 V, diode.i near 1.3e-13 A), where the discrete off flag is underdetermined: both labels give identical voltage and current, OMC records off=false (conducting at zero current) and rumoca off=true (blocking at zero voltage), while every continuous electrical quantity agrees. Pointwise comparison of the discrete flag is non-identifying at the knee.

All observed non-high channels are internal advancedSolenoid node voltages and half-coil across-voltages (r_par1.v, r_par2.v, r_2.p.v, coil1.n.v, coil2.v and sibling node potentials); no current, flux, force, inductance, position, or terminal channel deviates. They share an identical common-mode offset near 0.4544 V across nodes at very different levels, the signature of a floating internal sub-network whose half-coil voltage split the model regularizes only with 1 nF parasitic capacitors (their documented purpose is to keep the half-coil voltages well-defined). At the quasi-static 12 V operating point that regularization is weakest; the total coil EMF (coil1.v + coil2.v) and all terminal and resistive drops agree, only the weakly-determined split between the half-coils differs. Pointwise comparison of these internal voltages against OMC is non-identifying.
